{{Short description|Czech mathematician (1933–1989)}}
[[File:Zdenek Frolik.png|thumb|Zdeněk Frolík in 1971]]

'''Zdeněk Frolík''' (10 March 1933 – 3 May 1989) was a [[Czechs|Czech]] mathematician. His research interests included [[topology]] and [[functional analysis]]. In particular, his work concerned covering properties of topological spaces, ultrafilters, homogeneity, measures, uniform spaces. He was one of the founders of modern descriptive theory of sets and spaces.<ref>Zdeněk Frolík 1933–1989, [[Mirek Husek]], [[Jan Pelant]], ''[[Topology and its Applications]]'', Volume 44, issues 1–3, 22 May 1992, pp. 11–17,([http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/016686419290074A access on subscription]).</ref>

Two classes of topological spaces are given Frolík's name: the class P of all spaces <math>X</math> such that <math>X \times Y</math> is [[pseudocompact]] for every pseudocompact space <math>Y</math>,<ref>[[Jerry Vaughan|Vaughan, Jerry E.]], [http://dml.cz/dmlcz/128448 On Frolík's characterization of class ''P'']. ''Czechoslovak Mathematical Journal'', vol. 44 (1994), issue 1, pp. 1-6, freely available.</ref> and the class C of all spaces <math>X</math> such that <math>X \times Y</math> is [[countably compact]] for every countably compact space <math>Y</math>.<ref>J.E. Vaughan, Countably compact and sequentially compact spaces. ''Handbook of Set-theoretic Topology'', [[Kenneth Kunen|K. Kunen]] and J. Vaughan (ed.), [[North-Holland Publishing Company|North-Holland]], Amsterdam, 1984.</ref>

Frolík prepared his Ph.D. thesis under the supervision of [[Miroslav Katetov]] and [[Eduard Čech]].<ref>[http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=103809 Zdeněk Frolík] on the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]].</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Generalizations of compact and Lindelöf spaces - Czechoslovak Math. J., 9 (1959), pp.&nbsp;172–217 (in Russian, English summary)
*The topological product of countably compact spaces - Czechoslovak Math. J., 10 (1960), pp.&nbsp;329–338
*The topological product of two pseudocompact spaces - Czechoslovak Math. J., 10 (1960), pp.&nbsp;339–349
*Generalizations of the Gδ-property of complete metric spaces - Czechoslovak Math. J., 10 (1960), pp.&nbsp;359–379
*On the topological product of paracompact spaces - Bull. Acad. Polon., 8 (1960), pp.&nbsp;747–750
*Locally complete topological spaces - [[Proceedings of the USSR Academy of Sciences|Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR]], 137 (1961), pp.&nbsp;790–792 (in Russian)
*Applications of complete families of continuous functions to the theory of Q-spaces - Czechoslovak Math. J., 11 (1961), pp.&nbsp;115–133
*Invariance of Gδ-spaces under mappings - Czechoslovak Math. J., 11 (1961), pp.&nbsp;258–260
*On almost real compact spaces - Bull. Acad. Polon., 9 (1961), pp.&nbsp;247–250
*On two problems of W.W. Comfort - Comment. Math. Univ. Carolin., 7 (1966), pp.&nbsp;139–144
*Non-homogeneity of βP- P - Comment. Math. Univ. Carolin., 7 (1966), pp.&nbsp;705–710
*Sums of ultrafilters - Bull. Amer. Math. Soc., 73 (1967), pp.&nbsp;87–91
*Homogeneity problems for extremally disconnected spaces - Comment. Math. Univ. Carolin., 8 (1967), pp.&nbsp;757–763
*Baire sets that are Borelian subspaces - Proc. Roy. Soc. A, 299 (1967), pp.&nbsp;287–290
*On the Suslin-graph theorem - Comment Math. Univ. Carolin., 9 (1968), pp.&nbsp;243–249
*A survey of separable descriptive theory of sets and spaces - Czechoslovak Math. J., 20 (1970), pp.&nbsp;406–467
*A measurable map with analytic domain and metrizable range is quotient - Bull. Amer. Math. Soc., 76 (1970), pp.&nbsp;1112–1117
*Luzin sets are additive - Comment Math. Univ. Carolin., 21 (1980), pp.&nbsp;527–534
*Refinements of perfect maps onto metrizable spaces and an application to Čech-analytic spaces - Topology Appl., 33 (1989), pp.&nbsp;77–84
*Decomposability of completely Suslin additive families - Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 82 (1981), pp.&nbsp;359–365
*Applications of Luzinian separation principles (non-separable case) - Fund. Math., 117 (1983), pp.&nbsp;165–185
*Analytic and Luzin spaces (non-separable case) - [[Topology and its Applications|Topology Appl.]], 19 (1985), pp.&nbsp;129–156
